features.name: Extensions concept
features.description: Extensions were introduced in Navision 1993 as a way to add functionality without modifying core code. These bolt-on extensions used triggers to extend functionality separately from the underlying code.

features.name: App Store model
features.description: Partner ecosystem split in 1997 between Navision Solution Centers that sell product and Independent Software Houses that develop extensions for resale, creating an early app store model.

features.name: SaaS version of Navision
features.description: A SaaS version of Navision was demonstrated at the Microsoft Azure Summit in Abu Dhabi in 2014, representing early cloud strategy before Business Central.
caveats: This was SaaS version of Navision, not BC

features.name: Navision to BC transition model
features.description: By 2018, the business model shifted away from monolithic development focused on individual developer productivity toward distributed, consultancy-driven implementations with BC.

features.name: Value-based selling
features.description: Beginning in 1995, the industry shifted from hourly billing to value-based selling as a core business model change for partners.

features.name: Recurring revenue model for BC partners
features.description: Shift from licensing-based one-time revenue to ongoing monthly payments based on customer happiness. Partners invest risk upfront and customers pay continuously only while satisfied, replacing the legacy Navision upfront payment model.
caveats: Fixed price divided over months is not true recurring model
Requires shift from selling hours to selling products

features.name: Product-based BC partner model
features.description: Partners should sell vertical solutions and apps rather than custom services. The model involves blending customer requirements into average products that work for most customers rather than exceptional customizations for each.
caveats: Cannot serve all market segments equally
Must ignore exceptionally demanding and bland customers

features.name: Value-based pricing instead of cost-plus
features.description: BC partners should charge customers based on the value delivered rather than the cost incurred. Move away from calculating price based on partner labor costs and instead focus on customer outcomes and value received.
caveats: Difficult to shift established cost-plus mindset
Requires understanding customer value not partner cost

features.name: Outcomes-based delivery over hours
features.description: Partners should shift from selling billable hours to delivering repeatable outcomes. With outcomes-based systems, customer risk is stable and partners own the process efficiency, rather than charging for time spent.
caveats: Partners must absorb cost overruns
Requires highly repeatable processes

features.name: Faster project timelines benefit partner revenue
features.description: With recurring revenue models, partners make money only after go-live. The faster the go-live, the sooner revenue starts. This creates alignment where shorter project timelines increase partner revenue rather than the Navision model where longer projects meant more billable hours.
caveats: Requires end-to-end process efficiency
Depends on repeatable implementation methodology

features.name: Specialization required in BC partner teams
features.description: Partner teams must move from generalist 10X developers to specialized production lines. Future BC implementations will require 10-15 specialists even for basic systems, with each person contributing their specialty rather than all-around knowledge.
caveats: Significant organizational change required
Skills are changing too fast for generalists

features.name: Product manager cost tracking model
features.description: Shift from project manager billing timesheets to product manager tracking of product-wide costs including automated testing and quality assurance that customers don't directly pay for.
caveats: Less than 5% of partners have full control over this model
Only handful have truly adopted product manager approach

features.name: Continuous version updates model
features.description: Technical approach where everyone stays on the latest version to reduce technical debt from custom developments.
caveats: Technical skills required are being resolved well

features.name: Customer data ownership responsibility
features.description: Shift from partners cleaning customer data to customers ensuring data quality before import, with external audit verification.
caveats: Good for customer responsibility but may lead to employee burnout

features.name: Self-service customer support model
features.description: Business Central customers perform more self-service tasks like data cleanup and onboarding, shifting work from paid support to customer staff.
caveats: Causing employee burnout in customer organizations
Customers unaware of workload implications
Reduces paid support costs but increases internal customer work

features.name: Recurring monthly billing model
features.description: A shift from hourly time-and-materials billing to a fixed monthly subscription model for customers. Partners charge customers a consistent monthly fee per user for all support and services.
caveats: Requires mindset shift across entire partner organization
Demands upfront decision to commit to new model
Takes significant time to convert existing customer base

features.name: Timesheet elimination
features.description: Eliminating internal timesheet tracking systems when transitioning to recurring billing. Once customers convert to monthly billing, partners can remove the entire infrastructure for time tracking and project billing.
caveats: Requires full customer conversion to recurring model
Still requires timesheet systems until all customers are converted
Cannot be done selectively across different team members

features.name: Customer conversion strategy
features.description: A phased approach to converting existing customers from hourly billing to monthly recurring revenue. Approach involves selecting pilot customers, setting clear timelines, and gradually rolling out to remaining customers.
caveats: Process took 5 years but could be done in 1 year with proper knowledge
Initial delay between first and second customer conversion was over a year
Subsequent conversions became easier and faster
Conversion can be accelerated with proper strategy

quotes.text: the first time I saw a demonstration of extensions was in 1993
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that extensions concept predates BC by 30 years, making AL and extension-based architecture not a major change from Navision.

quotes.text: we have to break from hourly billing. We hourly billing is has no future, we have to start selling value.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows value-based selling was mandated 31 years ago, making the shift away from time sheets an old business model change not specific to BC.

quotes.text: 2018 was when we had that line where the Navision model had to die and the BC model came across
quotes.why_it_matters: Marks the critical inflection point where Navision's monolithic developer model ended and BC's consultancy-driven model began.

quotes.why_it_matters: Illustrates the shift from investing in deep tool mastery toward focusing on customer delivery as technology now changes weekly.

quotes.why_it_matters: Illustrates that investment in specific tools has short ROI windows in modern development, changing the approach partners should take to training.

quotes.text: We need to focus more on what we deliver to the customer and not the mechanism and the tools we use to get it
quotes.why_it_matters: Core philosophy shift: delivering customer value matters more than specific technical tools or skills.

quotes.why_it_matters: States the core shift: the BC partner takes the upfront risk instead of the customer.

quotes.text: Fixed price and recurring model are not the same.
quotes.why_it_matters: Distinguishes a true recurring revenue model from a fixed price spread over months.

quotes.why_it_matters: Clear definition of the required pricing paradigm shift from cost-based to value-based delivery.

quotes.why_it_matters: Illustrates the fundamental shift in partner team structure from generalists to specialists, a key difference in development models.
